item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 15, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
Special Advisor to the President of Brazil Celso Amorim will visit China from September 16 to 17. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will meet with him. CCTV: The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) closed in Beijing two days ago. It attracted nearly 100 countries and international organizations to exhibit and hold events. A host of new products and services made their debut, drawing widespread attention. Some say CIFTIS has become a window into China’s continued opening up. What is your comment? Guo Jiakun: “China Services” is a new calling card of China’s high-standard opening up. This year’s CIFTIS attracted over 1,830 offline exhibitors and over 5,300 online, reaching over 1,200 outcomes. A series of new technologies, new solutions and new achievements were exhibited in such areas as IT, financial technologies, digital health care, smart education and energy conservation and environmental protection, creating new opportunities for cooperation. China will continue to connect with the international market with premium services, promote outcome sharing through mutually beneficial cooperation, and bring “China Services” to more countries, delivering greater benefit to the world. Kyodo News: The cross-party Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union had a meeting with Assistant Foreign Minister Liu Bin yesterday. Can you share more details and how does China view the significance of this talk? Guo Jiakun: On September 14, Assistant Foreign Minister Liu Bin met with the delegation of young Japanese lawmakers from the Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union, who was on a visit to China. China stressed that the crux of the serious difficulties in China-Japan relations lies in Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi’s erroneous words and deeds on Taiwan. The Japanese side should honor the spirit of the four political documents, learn the lesson of history, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. We hope that the Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union will carry forward its tradition of goodwill toward China, step up to its responsibility, and create conditions and a sound environment for bringing the bilateral relations back to the right track. Global Times: It is reported that in a statement issued on September 11, the Philippines’ Department of Foreign Affairs reaffirms the Philippines’ sovereign rights and jurisdiction over Meiji Jiao and Zhubi Jiao as low-tide elevations (LTE) within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. Later, it changed the narrative, reaffirming its sovereignty over Zhubi Jiao as an LTE within the territorial sea of Zhongye Dao. The statement claims that China’s island-building on the above-mentioned features violates the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, UNCLOS and the 2016 Arbitral Award. Does China have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: Nansha Qundao, including Meiji Jiao, Zhubi Jiao and Zhongye Dao, are China’s inherent territory. It is totally legitimate and lawful for China to conduct construction and other activities on its own territory, a matter within China’s sovereignty. The territorial scope of the Philippines has already been defined by a series of international treaties. Nansha Qundao has never been part of the Philippine territory. According to the “land dominates the sea” principle in international law, the Philippines’ claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China’s territory is illegal. The Philippine side at one point claimed that Zhubi Jiao is within its EEZ and continental shelf, but later claimed that it lies within the territorial sea of the island it illegally occupies. This only exposes how absurd and random its claim is, making it totally untenable. The “South China Sea arbitration” is completely a political manipulation by the Philippines to grab unlawful gains. The so-called “award” is illegal, null and void, and has no binding force. The Philippines’ so-called “Maritime Zones Act” illegally includes China’s Huangyan Dao and most of the islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao and relevant waters into the Philippines’ maritime zone. This is a grave violation of China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea, and is illegal and null and void. China firmly opposes it and will never accept it. Let me stress once again: China will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and firmly oppose any infringement. The Philippines should immediately stop infringing upon China’s rights, and stop the provocations and publicity stunts. AFP: An official from the U.S. military said yesterday that the U.S. is facing a shortfall in ammunition as a result of its war in Iran. Does China have any comment on this? Guo Jiakun: China is following the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region. We hope that relevant parties will resolve disputes through political and diplomatic means. AFP: The U.S. Space Force said yesterday that the United States has weapons deployed in space. What is China’s reaction? Does China also have weapons deployed in space? Guo Jiakun: China stands for peaceful use of outer space and keeping it safe, and opposes any arms race in outer space or any attempt to weaponize it and turn it into a warzone. We urge the U.S. to stop expanding military build-up in outer space, and uphold global strategic stability with concrete actions. China News Service: According to reports, on September 14, the China National Space Administration, the Permanent Mission of China to the United Nations and Other International Organizations in Vienna, and the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs held a ceremony at the UN Headquarters in Vienna where China formally gifted the United Nations with the world’s first soil sample collected from the far side of the moon by the Chang’e‑6 mission. Ms. Monica Juma, Director‑General of the United Nations Office at Vienna, said that the permanent display of the lunar sample at the United Nations Office in Vienna is of great significance, adding that it demonstrates China’s support for the United Nations in galvanizing efforts in the international community to address common challenges. Would you like to comment on this? Is China trying to share its vision for space exploration through this gift? Guo Jiakun: By donating to the United Nations a soil sample collected from the far side of the moon by the Chang’e‑6 mission, China is delivering on the four major global initiatives put forward by President Xi Jinping. The move demonstrates China’s firm support for the United Nations and multilateralism as well as its sense of responsibility as a major country on the peaceful use of outer space and improving global space governance. China looks forward to working with all countries to uphold relevant international law with the Outer Space Treaty as the cornerstone, abide by the paramount principle of exploring and using outer space for peaceful purposes, firmly oppose attempts to weaponize space or turn it into a battlefield, make sure progress in science and technology will bring greater benefits to all humanity, and ensure that space will truly become a platform for win‑win cooperation. ************************************************** The following question was raised by Bloomberg after the press conference: Can the foreign ministry clarify and elaborate on your response yesterday regarding calls from U.S. tech leaders for a slowing down AI development. How does China assess the risks posed by AI including the possibility of AI being used for the production of biological weapons? Guo Jiakun: We noted recent remarks by some in the U.S. AI industry. As AI develops at an incredible speed, it’s all the more important to stay committed to developing AI for the positive, for good, and for the benefits of the people, to calibrate regulation and governance on AI, and to promptly strengthen safeguards to prevent it from getting out of control. China puts equal emphasis on development and security in terms of AI. We take seriously the inherent and secondary risks of AI. We are committed to holding on to the bottom line of security, and we have been making continued efforts to improve laws and regulations, policies, application norms, and ethic rules to prevent the abuse and misuse of AI, and ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable. Yesterday, Chinese relevant authorities released AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0, in which the classification of AI safety risks was reviewed and updated, and recommendations on optimizing technological countermeasures and comprehensive governance measures were outlined. AI is the collective wisdom and precious asset shared by all humanity. AI development and governance require the practice of true multilateralism, with all countries working together to build a global governance framework on broad-based consensus. No single country or enterprise can develop effective solutions on its own. China always supports the UN’s role as the main channel in global AI governance, and participates in the multilateral governance of AI in a responsible attitude. China stands ready to join hands with all countries to build a just and equitable system for global AI governance, and develop AI for good and for all.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 14, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
CGTN: President Xi Jinping just concluded his trip to New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit. Can you share more details? China will take over the BRICS chairship next year. What role does China hope to play in advancing BRICS cooperation? Guo Jiakun: From September 12 to 13, President Xi Jinping attended the 18th BRICS Summit in India upon invitation. He attended Session I and Session II of the summit, delivered important statements, and had discussions with leaders of other BRICS member states to chart the course for a new chapter of development and cooperation. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. President Xi Jinping summarized the course of BRICS development with three phrases: self-reliance and self-strengthening, standing together through wind and rain, and fruitful outcomes. He pointed out that over the past two decades, BRICS has been growing with strong vigor and vitality, and become the most influential cooperation platform in today’s world for emerging markets and developing countries. President Xi Jinping stressed that BRICS must stand firmly on the right side of history, and strive to be a pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development, a pioneer in upholding peace and stability, a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations, and a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, hold high the banner of multilateralism, stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy, jointly advance security governance, steer the international order in a direction that is more just and equitable, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. President Xi Jinping pointed out that to accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented. During the summit, President Xi Jinping proposed several initiatives, including the open source and inclusive AI initiative, the digital industry cooperation initiative, and the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative. He announced multiple practical cooperation measures, in particular, China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, establish a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation. China is committed to supporting other Global South countries in improving capacity and benefiting equally from emerging technologies so as to thrive together. China will take over the BRICS chairship next year, and host the 19th BRICS Summit. The Chinese side will build consensus and work with all parties to plan for the future. Together, we will usher in the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, and open up a bright prospect of shared prosperity and progress. Xinhua News Agency: On September 12, President Xi Jinping met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi while attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, extending their annual meeting arrangement into the third year. Could you talk about the new consensus the two leaders reached on China-India relations during this meeting? Guo Jiakun: Indeed, this was President Xi and Prime Minister Modi’s third meeting in three years. The meeting in New Delhi marks the two leaders “reaffirmation” of the growth of China-India ties after guiding the bilateral relations from starting afresh in Kazan to making further improvements in Tianjin. The most important consensus reached is that China and India should be partners. As President Xi noted, China and India have different national realities. We should draw on each other’s strengths, support each other, help each other succeed, and develop together. To promote the steady and sustained development of China-India relations, both sides need to calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic perception, help each other succeed in the spirit of win-win cooperation, remove irritants with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, and contribute to a better world with open and inclusive multilateral coordination. Prime Minister Modi said that India has an independent foreign policy, developing relations with China is not affected by any third party and that it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities on its territory. China values Prime Minister Modi’s statements. The two leaders agreed that as the most populous countries in the world and major members of the Global South, China and India should focus on development, which is the biggest common denominator, strengthen friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation, and improve public perception of the bilateral relations. The two sides should also address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the sound and steady development of economic and trade relations. The two sides agreed to support each other in chairing BRICS, promote cooperation in the Global South, help build a multipolar world, and serve as forces for progress and stability in the volatile world. At the same time, the two leaders agreed to properly handle the disputes and disagreements between China and India to jointly safeguard peace and tranquility in the border area. The improvement and development of China-India relations is not only welcomed by the 2.8 billion people of the two countries, but also the right thing to do to enhance the cooperation in the Global South. As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders, make the cooperation list longer, deepen people-to-people exchanges, have closer collaboration on multilateral occasions, make continued efforts to improve and grow our ties, and render firm support to each other’s development and revitalization, so that we can contribution to the peace and prosperity in the region and beyond. Reuters: The Wall Street Journal reported over the weekend that Iran acquired satellite images of the U.S. base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three U.S. troops there in July. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on The Wall Street Journal’s report? Guo Jiakun: China always strictly fulfills its due international obligations. We oppose exploiting the conflict to throw mud at China. Phoenix TV: Yemen’s Houthis recently attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia, injuring more than 70 civilians and damaging multiple energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure. The Houthis said that they had also come under attack and suffered casualties. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China is deeply concerned about the casualties of innocent civilians and the damage to energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure caused by recent escalation in Yemen and the Red Sea. Attacks against civilian infrastructure that bears on people’s livelihoods are unacceptable. Increasing turmoil in the region serves no one’s interest. The sovereignty and security of all countries should be respected, and the only viable way forward is to resolve disputes through political and diplomatic means. China calls on the relevant parties to exercise restraint, ease tensions through communication and dialogue and work toward deescalation as soon as possible. Reuters: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk all over the weekend called on AI companies to slow down frontier development, with Amodei arguing a Chinese advantage in AI would pose U.S. national security risks. Does the foreign ministry have any comment? Guo Jiakun: AI is a consequential technology for the wellbeing of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only hamper efforts toward sound global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest. Antara: At the recent BRICS Summit, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto called on BRICS member states to pursue joint industrialization, noting that each member already constitutes an important part of global supply chains. He argued that closer industrial cooperation would enable member states to generate greater added value. Does the ministry have any comment on President Prabowo’s proposal? Guo Jiakun: For many years, BRICS has been actively promoting cooperation on industrialization, evidenced by the establishment of BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center and BRICS Center for Industrial Competences, and marked by a great number of practical outcomes. China will strengthen technological cooperation with BRICS countries, deepen industrial alignment, carry out capacity-building projects, and achieve more sustainable development featured by higher quality and greater resilience. China News Service: It’s reported that the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Awareness Week was held in Jinan, Shandong Province today. The theme of the week is “Cybersecurity for the People, Cybersecurity by the People – Safeguarding the Smart Era with Cybersecurity.” Can you share China’s thinking for holding the event? What China believes countries should do to jointly safeguard cybersecurity in the age of intelligence? Guo Jiakun: The internet connects households across the world. A peaceful, safe and secure, open and cooperative cyberspace is of great significance for all countries in the world. Since 2014, China has held the annual National Cybersecurity Awareness Week to improve public awareness and capability on cybersecurity, foster a healthy and positive environment in cyberspace, and provide China’s useful experience for global governance in cyberspace. As we speak, emerging technologies, notably AI, is profoundly reshaping the cyberspace. As a firm defender of cybersecurity, China has officially put AI under the supervision of national cybersecurity laws and regulations, and has been improving relevant institutional guidelines and ethical norms. We stand ready to continue working with the rest of the world to actively respond to cybersecurity risks and challenges in the intelligence age, promote the building of a community with a shared future in cyberspace, and enable the internet to better benefit the people of all countries. China Daily: It’s reported that some Panamanian lawmakers recently set up a so-called “Panama-Taiwan parliamentary exchange group.” U.S. lawmakers attended the launch of the group via video link. Regarding this, Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino stated that the Panamanian government reiterates that “foreign relations are directed by the Executive,” and engagements of the parliamentarians with Taiwan “do not mean that the Executive endorses them.” Do you have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: There is but one China in the world and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. China firmly opposes official interactions and engagements of any form between the Taiwan authorities and countries having diplomatic ties with China, and does not allow interference in China’s internal affairs by any external forces. We urge those few politicians to see the real picture. To cross the line on the Taiwan question will lead to serious consequences. The establishment of this so-called “parliamentary exchange group” seriously violates the one-China principle upheld by Panama. We noted the statement of the Panamanian government and hopes that Panama will honor its commitment to the one-China principle with real actions to uphold the political foundation of China-Panama relations. China urges the U.S. to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, stop sending the wrong message to “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, and stop disrupting and sabotaging China-Panama relations. Reuters: Are you able to provide an update on the status of the search mission for missing foreign nationals from the flood in Tibet and Nepal? Whether the Chinese government is in touch with Apple or other smart device makers to help locate those unaccounted for? Guo Jiakun: We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China of the procedures for DNA information collection from relatives of the missing foreign nationals. Once the remains of any foreign national are found and after the identity is confirmed, the relevant embassy will be contacted to communicate follow-up arrangements. The Xizang Autonomous Region authorities have opened a hotline for families of the missing foreign nationals and will provide them with timely assistance. The Paper: Not long ago, the MFA hosted events under the theme “Explore People-Centered Cities: China’s Governance, Global Engagement” in Shanghai and Jiangsu, as part of the program of the “Beyond the Capital” diplomatic tour. In the first half of this year, the MFA also hosted events under the theme “Set Sail for the 15th Five-Year Plan: China’s Growth, World’s Opportunity.” Could you share more details and China’s consideration of launching these two new programs? Guo Jiakun: The “Beyond the Capital” diplomatic tour, a flagship program which enables diplomatic service to empower development across the country, provides a hands-on opportunity for foreign diplomats in China to have a deeper understanding of China. The events you mentioned are exactly the upgraded version of the program, with a focus on development and governance. The trip to the Pearl River Delta helps explore the vitality of development and cooperation opportunities unleashed by the 15th Five-Year Plan. The trip to the Yangtze River Delta centers on urban governance and offers an opportunity to witness how China puts into practice its people-centered development philosophy. Participating diplomatic envoys noted that, the events serve not only as an opportunity to better understand China, but also a platform for governance experience sharing and mutual learning among countries with different cultural traditions and in different stage of development. We welcome more diplomatic envoys to join the events. DPA: Russian news agency TASS reported that Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters in New Delhi that Indian and Chinese leaders asked detailed questions about a settlement in Ukraine and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution. Can the foreign ministry confirm this? How would China help find a solution in the ongoing war in Ukraine? Guo Jiakun: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis has been consistent and clear. We always believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the crisis, and support all efforts for peace.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 11, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
People’s Daily: The Chinese side has announced that President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th BRICS Summit. Could you share China’s expectations for this event? Mao Ning: BRICS is the key platform for solidarity and cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. Guided by the BRICS Spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation, BRICS countries have been committed to upholding multilateralism, defending fairness and justice, and pursuing common development ever since the grouping was formed. Today, BRICS has grown into a real force standing at the forefront of the Global South. China sets great store by and actively participates in BRICS cooperation. President Xi will attend and address the upcoming summit, have in-depth exchanges with other leaders on major issues including the current international situation, the development of BRICS mechanisms, and deepening practical cooperation, and put forward China’s important initiatives and propositions, charting the course for the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. China is ready to work with fellow BRICS countries for steady and sustained progress in greater BRICS cooperation to contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity. AFP: U.S. artificial intelligence firm Anthropic said in a report yesterday that it has shut down multiple operations that are believed to be linked to the Chinese government. The report said that the actors were using its chatbot Claude to gather information on various targets, including overseas religious communities, Uyghurs in Syria and Chinese diaspora groups. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China advocates AI for good. We firmly oppose attempts to throw mud at China by distorting facts. Shenzhen TV: According to WIPO’s latest Global Innovation Index, China leads the innovation cluster count for a fourth consecutive year with 25 top 100 innovation clusters. Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou tops the global rankings for a second consecutive year. Some say innovation has become a major driver of China’s development and the world should recognize the dividends and opportunities generated by China’s innovation. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: I noticed the announced rankings. Innovation is key to China’s sustained economic performance and soaring industrial competitiveness. Chinese innovation creates opportunities for all countries. More and more foreign firms choose to do R&D and innovate in China and excel in global competition by tapping into China’s mega-market. For China, innovation is never about monopoly. We are committed to sharing innovation dividends with the world to thrive together. The Hindu: Another question on President Xi’s visit to India for the BRICS Summit. This will also be the first meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Modi since Tianjin last year. What are China’s expectations for this meeting between the two leaders and what role does Beijing see this meeting between the leaders is having on the ongoing normalization in relations? Mao Ning: China and India are arranging for the bilateral meeting between President Xi and Prime Minister Modi. This will be the third year in a row for the two leaders to meet with each other, following their meetings in Kazan and Tianjin. China will work with India to act on the strategic guidance of the two leaders, handle the bilateral relations from a strategic height and long-term perspective, step up communication, enhance cooperation, properly handle differences, and be friends enjoying good-neighborliness and partners helping each other succeed. PTI: Can you please share some details about President Xi’s delegation? How many members? There are reports that it is quite a large delegation, especially quite a number of heads of businesses are going to attend the BRICS Business Forum. Second question, this BRICS Summit is a bit different, as it is taking place amid two bitter conflicts, one in the Middle East and another is the Ukraine-Russia conflict. To stretch further, can you elaborate more on what China’s expectations as well as China’s priorities are as far as this particular BRICS Summit in Delhi? Mao Ning: On your first question, there will be timely updates on President Xi Jinping’s trip to India for the BRICS Summit. On your second question, China advocates a common, comprehensive, cooperative, and sustainable approach to security. We are committed to promoting the political settlement of hotspot issues through dialogue. We look forward to working with fellow BRICS countries to promote dialogue and negotiation to resolve differences and jointly safeguard regional and global peace and stability. Reuters: The Taiwanese official Hsiao Bi-khim is in Italy. Does China have a response to this? Mao Ning: China has lodged serious protests with Italy and the EU side on the “Taiwan independence” politicians’ attendance at the conference in Italy. The DPP authorities and individual politicians from Taiwan are making every attempt to grab attention and solicit external support for their separatist agenda under the pretext of “democracy” and “freedom.” Their moves are truly despicable and simply futile. Let me reiterate that there is but one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. China firmly opposes official interactions of any form between China’s Taiwan region and countries having diplomatic ties with China. The one-China principle is a widely-recognized norm in international relations and a prevailing international consensus. It is also the political foundation of China-Italy relations and China-EU relations. We urge relevant parties to honor the one-China principle with real action. CCTV: We noted that individual politicians from the U.S. and other Western countries have repeatedly expressed so-called “concern” over the “Hong Kong Alliance” case. Today, a Hong Kong court announced the sentence regarding the case. What is your comment? Mao Ning: China has made clear its just position on the “Hong Kong Alliance” case. The rule of law is upheld in Hong Kong. The central government firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in lawfully safeguarding national security and fighting activities endangering national security. Relevant parties need to earnestly respect China’s sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, stop making irresponsible remarks on the SAR’s handling of judicial cases, and stop interfering in Hong Kong’s judicial affairs, which are China’s internal affairs, in any form. Kyodo News: Could you please comment on China’s announcement to increase visa fees for Japanese citizens travelling to China? Mao Ning: The Chinese Embassy in Japan has issued a notice. The adjustment was made based on the principle of reciprocity. Reuters: The Kremlin’s Aide Yuri Ushakov said on Tuesday that the three heads of state of China, the U.S. and Russia may hold a trilateral meeting at the next APEC Forum in November. Can China confirm or comment on this? Mao Ning: I don’t have any information to provide. Bloomberg: South Korea is tightening its defenses against industrial espionage with the revised law taking effect this weekend. China is not explicitly mentioned in the revised law, but half of all detective cases involving leaks of sensitive technology to foreign entities last year involve China, according to the South Korean police. What’s the Chinese foreign ministry’s comment on these new rules? Mao Ning: The Chinese government always asks Chinese enterprises to abide by international rules and relevant laws and regulations in conducting international cooperation. Countries are expected to protect normal investment and business operations and provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 10, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
AFP: Will Chinese leader travel to India this weekend for the BRICS Summit? Guo Jiakun: On this question, I have no information to share at the moment. Reuters: India’s Serious Fraud Office has recommended that China’s Xiaomi be investigated for alleged irregularities in its business model and compliance with foreign investment law. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China-India economic and trade cooperation is mutually beneficial in nature. We hope India will provide a fair, just, transparent and non-discriminatory environment for the investment and operation of companies of all countries in India. NBC: At his meeting with the U.S. Ambassador David Perdue the other week, Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged both sides to “eliminate interference and overcome obstacles” for high-level engagements between the two countries. Is there any example of “obstacle” that the Chinese side believes is within the U.S. ability to tackle or otherwise, in general, are both sides, from their most recent communications, making some progress in dealing with these “obstacles”? Guo Jiakun: China released a readout on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s meeting with U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to bilateral relations. China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state within the year. Global Times: It is reported that in a media briefing, the U.S. embassy in Panama introduced a pilot AI supply chain credentialing and provenance platform in Panama, the first of its kind in the world. The U.S. said the project was under evaluation. Some media commented that by verifying the origin, custody, and compliance status of cargo for AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and critical minerals, the project in essence serves the U.S. control of tech industrial and supply chains and tech blockade of China. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: We noticed relevant reports. The development of AI bears on the common welfare of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Exclusive groupings and geopolitical calculations are not conducive to technological development and progress in LAC countries and the rest of the Global South. China will work with LAC countries and other parties to jointly build a just and equitable global AI governance system, and develop AI for the good of people worldwide. Reuters: Nepal is planning to ask wealthier countries and agencies for financial help this week. It has said that they should contribute to the US$5 billion that’s needed for the rebuilding following the flooding. Has Nepal asked China for financial help and does China have any plans to contribute? Guo Jiakun: After the sudden mudslide struck the China-Nepal border areas, while urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. China and Nepal are traditional friends and close neighbors. We stand ready to assist Nepal in post-disaster reconstruction to the best of our capability based on its needs. We believe the Nepali people will overcome difficulties and rebuild their homes soon under the leadership of their government.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Xinhua News Agency: We noted recent comments saying China only cares for its own development while “pulling up the ladder” for the development of other Global South countries. What is your comment? Mao Ning: China never pulls up the ladder from any country. Rather, China has long been building up ladders so that countries could reach higher together. Through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, for instance, China has been helping partner countries bridge the infrastructure gap. By providing Global South countries with affordable industrial equipment and tech products and sharing experience and expertise, China has helped lower the cost for these countries’ industrial growth. China’s zero-tariff policy and “Export to China” initiative generate profits and market opportunities that enable Global South countries to better integrate into the global supply chains and enhance growth resilience. For China, cooperation with other countries has always been about mutual success. The “pulling-up-the-ladder” narrative has zero resonance with Global South countries. China will always pursue mutual benefit and common development, be a reliable partner of Global South countries, and contribute to the prosperity of the Global South through China’s own development. AFP: U.S. cyber security firm Calif said yesterday that it has built an AI-assisted hacking tool that can access the personal accounts and private information on the Chinese app WeChat. Tencent has said that the security risk has been fixed after being notified by Calif. But as a matter of cyber security, does the foreign ministry have comments on this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China stands for promoting AI for good and preventing the abuse and malicious use of AI. AFP: Yesterday, the U.S. Cyber Defense Agency accused top Chinese AI labs, including DeepSeek and Moonshot of stealing the capabilities of U.S. models. It said that these campaigns “form the core” of China-based AI companies’ strategies. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this? Mao Ning: The development of AI in China comes from greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and is fueled by China’s vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit and commitment to open cooperation. We believe all parties need to make sure AI development is open and inclusive and promotes the well-being of humanity as a force for good and for all. We hope the U.S. side will earnestly act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and stop leveling false allegations to smear China. As two major powers in AI, China and the U.S. should step up cooperation. NHK: The BRICS Summit will be held in India this weekend. Who will lead the Chinese delegation? Mao Ning: We will release timely information if there is any update. Please stay tuned. AFP: At an international forum yesterday, the Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilberto Teodoro Jr. criticized what he called a violation of UNCLOS and “coercion, bullying and aggression” by China in response to him being handed a piece of paper stating China’s position on the South China Sea. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on the situation or a response to the remarks by the Philippines’ Defense Secretary? Mao Ning: I’m not sure what exactly happened at the event, but China’s position has always been clear on the so-called “South China Sea arbitration”. The Philippines unilaterally initiated the case, which is a distortion and abuse of the UNCLOS dispute settlement mechanism. It is the Philippine side who has violated UNCLOS and undermined its integrity and authority. We urge the certain individual of the Philippine side to cut the provocations and theatrics, and stop undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 8, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
CCTV: Could you update us on China’s assistance for Nepal’s disaster relief efforts? Mao Ning: To support Nepal’s rescue and relief efforts, China sent out this morning the fourth batch of emergency relief supplies, including equipment for transportation and lighting and mortuary supplies. Across China, help is on the way to Nepal. China Foundation for Rural Development has sent people to the affected communities in Nepal to set up temporary shelters and provide daily necessities and basic medical services. The Chinese Enterprises Association in Nepal recently delivered the first batch of funds donated for relief operations. China will continue standing firmly with Nepal to overcome this challenging time together. RT: The Japanese government recently asked Russia to remove a monument commemorating the victory over Japan’s militarism, saying that this issue affects the feelings of the Japanese people. And Japan also claimed that the “Enemy State Clauses” in the UN Charter are obsolete. How does China view these comments made by the Japanese government on WWII history and postwar international order? Mao Ning: To view and treat history correctly is a key gauge of Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. Japan joined the UN after admitting to its militarist crimes and recognizing the UN Charter in its entirety. The “Enemy State Clauses” in the Charter, a special set of rules for WWII defeated states, are still valid today. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. The Japanese side should use history as a mirror, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. China-Arab TV: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China from September 7 to 8. Can you elaborate on the goals and significance of this visit? Specifically, how does China view the timing of this visit, and what are the outcomes of the bilateral talks? Mao Ning: China and Qatar are strategic partners. China highly values its relations with Qatar. Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China. Yesterday, Premier Li Qiang met with him for in-depth exchange of views on issues of mutual interest. China looks to the visit as an opportunity to work for new progress in bilateral relations. On more details about the visit, we will release timely readouts. Please check back for updates. Beijing Youth Daily: We noted that China is hosting a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Beijing. Could you share with us more details? What’s China’s view on AI capacity-building? Mao Ning: At the 2026 World AI Conference & High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, President Xi Jinping announced that in the next five years, China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs. To ensure its early implementation, China is hosting once again a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Peking University from September 7 to 12. As part of the continued efforts to implement the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, China established the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, in an effort to make relevant technologies and services more accessible, and help Global South countries find a path to AI development suited to their needs. We will work with various parties to make AI a lasting source of benefits and a major driving force for the welfare of all humanity. AFP: India is scheduled to host a BRICS summit this weekend. Can the foreign ministry confirm who will be attending on China’s behalf? Secondly, what are China’s expectations for this BRICS summit? Mao Ning: China sets great store by BRICS cooperation. We support India in hosting a successful BRICS summit this year. For your specific questions, I don’t have more information to offer at the moment. China Daily: It’s reported that Lai Ching-te claimed at an event that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758. Taiwan is a “sovereign independent nation.” The resolution only addresses the People’s Republic of China’s representation at the UN and has nothing to do with Taiwan. What is China’s comment on this? Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. This is an unshakable fact grounded in both history and law. The Cairo Declaration issued by China, the U.S. and the UK in 1943 stated in explicit terms that Taiwan is a territory that Japan had stolen and shall be restored to China. The Potsdam Proclamation in 1945 reaffirmed that the terms of the Cairo Declaration shall be carried out. This series of instruments with legal effect under international law have all clearly affirmed China’s sovereignty over Taiwan. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which “decides to restore all its rights to the People’s Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations.” From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN. It made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as “two Chinas” or “one China, one Taiwan.” Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country. The Lai Ching-te authorities’ deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for “Taiwan independence.” Their rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community’s steadfast commitment to one China.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 7, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
CGTN: We noted that a delegation from the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) visited China and inspected facilities for the disposal of Japan’s abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs). Could you please provide more information on the visit? Mao Ning: From August 31 to September 5, the Director-General of the OPCW, the Chairperson of the Executive Council, as well as permanent representatives and senior diplomats from 12 countries to the OPCW, visited China upon invitation. During the visit, they travelled to Hunchun, Dunhua and Haerbaling in Jilin Province to inspect the excavation, recovery and destruction of Japan’s ACWs. The delegation’s visit coincided with China’s annual commemoration of the victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Japan’s militarist aggression inflicted immense humanitarian catastrophes on China and left behind the menace of ACWs. Through the visit, the delegation gained a deeper understanding of the grave harm posed by Japan’s ACWs to the lives and property of the Chinese people and to the country’s ecological environment, and expressed support for the OPCW, in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, in urging the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its obligations by completely and thoroughly destroying its ACWs in China without further delay, so as to restore a safe habitat for the Chinese people at an early date and realize the noble goal of a world free of chemical weapons as envisaged by the Convention. Reuters: We spoke to the Philippines’ defense secretary earlier today and he said China could use recently scaled-down U.S.-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to assert itself in the Indo-Pacific region. Do you have anything to say to that comment? Mao Ning: China is always committed to maintaining peace and stability in the Asia Pacific, and does not engage in major-country confrontation. We hope other regional countries will also play a positive role for peace and stability in the region. China News Service: According to the Solomon Star, Taiwan increased its annual aid to Palau from US$18 million last year to US$25 million this year, apparently in an effort to secure political backing at the Pacific Islands Forum. The Taiwan authorities also allocated nearly US$281,000 in direct cash gifts for Palau’s former president, incumbent political figures, and individual lawmakers. The report commented that Taiwan’s taxpayers’ hard-earned money is not being spent on people’s livelihoods. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: The report is yet another example of the Lai Ching-te authorities’ expensive dollar diplomacy using the hard-earned money of the people in Taiwan—a combination of corruption, fraudulence, bribery and power-for-money deals—to serve “Taiwan independence” separatism and their personal political agenda. For certain countries like Palau, having Taiwan as a “diplomatic ally” is not about delivering for the country and the people, but to line the pockets of the very few people who profit from it. EFE: Venezuela says its agreements with China will be respected and Chinese joint ventures will continue operating. Has Caracas given Beijing specific assurances that Chinese oil interests will not be affected by the new U.S.-Venezuela agreement? Mao Ning: Cooperation between China and Venezuela is under the protection of international law and laws of both countries. It has nothing to do with any third party and should not be disrupted by any third party. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected. AFP: The United States and China will hold talks on AI safety risks in coming weeks. This is according to a recent report by Reuters. Can the foreign ministry confirm these talks? They will reportedly take place in mid-September. What are Chinese expectations for these discussions? Mao Ning: China and the U.S. maintain communication on AI. DPA: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won the election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. In an interview with Phoenix TV, the AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund said that for Germany’s better development in the future, Germany needs China from a long-term perspective. What’s China’s take on this election result? Will China enhance communication with the AfD? Mao Ning: Regional elections in Germany are its domestic affair. China will not comment on that. China’s position on developing its relations with Germany is consistent. The Paper: We’ve learned that a group of foreign journalists were allowed by China to gain access to the disaster-hit area in Gyirong for interviews. Can you share more details on that? Mao Ning: The mudslide in Gyirong has drawn close attention from the international media, who hope to enter the area for reporting and interviews. With roads having just been cleared after non-stop repair work, China invited journalists from eight foreign media outlets, including the NBC, CNN, Reuters, RT and PTI, to enter the core area to learn about the impact of the disaster and progress in rescue, recovery and reconstruction. They also attended the group interview for journalists held by Xizang Autonomous Region. I believe you have seen the media reports from these outlets. China will continue its all-out search and rescue efforts to deal with the aftermath. We will provide timely updates on the situation on the ground and rescue operations.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Japanese Politicians Paying Respects to the Yasukuni War Shrine Which Honors Class-A War Criminals
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-15
Q: August 15 marks the day of Japan’s unconditional surrender in the Second World War. Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni war shrine today, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine. What’s your comment? A: China strongly deplores Japan’s negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan. During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes. The Yasukuni war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism. It is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression. No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians’ true intention which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan’s war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization. This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. To view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan’s ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions.
